samples.summary: A transient API error in gate 1 / gate 2 now terminates the autonomous loop permanently (sticky page + `agent:blocked`), where it previously retried next round — and neither read has any retry
samples.evidence: `ciPassed` (mark-ready.mjs:175-189) and `reviewChecks` (mark-ready.mjs:300-310) changed `catch { return false }` into `process.exit(2)`. Exit 2 is handled by the promote job's `2)` branch (agent-review-panel.yml:1543) with `exit 2`, which fails the `promote` job. `stalled` (agent-review-panel.yml:2309-2331) fires on `needs.promote.result == 'failure'` and posts `<!-- agent-review-paged -->` plus "The review panel will not run again on this PR" (line 2416), and the following reconcile step latches `agent:blocked`. So ANY single failed `gh api` call — a 5xx, a secondary-rate-limit, a network blip — now ends the loop for that PR until a human runs `@claude rerun`, whereas before it was a benign exit 1 ("leaving as draft") that the next CI-green round re-evaluated. These calls go through `execFileSync("gh", …)` with no retry, while the same file's workflow adds `retries: 3` to every `github-script` step precisely because "one transient 5xx anywhere is fatal" (agent-review-panel.yml:915-931 documents a 4-minute 503 outage that killed three panel runs). The distinction the new comment claims to make ("the CI workflow may have been renamed" = should page) is not actually made in code: a 404 and a 503 take the identical exit-2 path.

samples.summary: Gate 1b's page bound refuses a PR with exactly 1000 changed files, the off-by-one its own comment says it avoids
samples.evidence: `for (let page = 1; page <= 10; page++)` with `per_page=100` and `if (files.length < 100) return hits;`. A PR with exactly 1000 files returns 100 on every one of pages 1..10, so no page is short, the loop exits and `throw new Error("more than 1000 changed files …")` fires — refusing promotion for a PR whose list WAS fully enumerated. The comment immediately above (lines 207-209) states the opposite: "10 full pages is 1000 files enumerated, so the throw below is reached only by a PR with MORE than that — an off-by-one here would refuse a PR with exactly 1000." Honouring the comment needs one more iteration (`page <= 11`) or a short-page check after page 10. Fail-closed, so the cost is bounded, but code and its stated contract disagree.

samples.summary: Gate 1b makes promotion permanently impossible for a class of ordinary PRs but reports it as the retryable "a gate was not satisfied", so such a PR loops (re-paying for a full panel per round) and never pages
samples.evidence: `ciDefinitionGate` refuses any PR touching `package.json`, `packages/*/package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `knip.json`, `harness.config.json` (checks.mjs:123-135) — i.e. every dependency bump the agent itself can push. The refusal returns `false`, mark-ready exits 1, the promote job's `1)` branch (agent-review-panel.yml:1541) records `outcome=gates-unsatisfied`, and loop-status prints "a ready gate was not satisfied — the PR stays a draft" (line 1577), which is the same message used for the transient "CI not green yet" case. Nothing distinguishes "will be promotable after the next green CI" from "can NEVER be promoted by this pipeline", nothing pages, and the panel re-runs on every subsequent CI-green push, so the PR sits as a draft indefinitely while re-paying for review rounds. The intended remedy ("a human reviews the change and flips it to ready by hand", mark-ready.mjs:26-28) is never signalled as such to a human.

samples.summary: Re-running the newest COMPLETED run while a newer run is in flight can re-engage a panel for a superseded run and cancel the live one via the shared `active` concurrency group
samples.evidence: The new selection deliberately skips in-flight runs and re-runs the newest completed one (`agent-loop.yml:156-161`, `agent-rerun.yml:200-205`). Previously `per_page: 1` picked the newest run, so with a newer run in flight `reRunWorkflow` answered 422 and nothing happened. Now the older run is re-run; when it finishes it emits `completed` with `run_attempt > 1`, which the panel gate admits (agent-review-panel.yml:163-167) and which takes the `active` concurrency group (line 117) with `cancel-in-progress: true` — cancelling the panel the newer run started on `requested`, potentially mid-`fix`-push, which is the exact failure the surrounding comment says the one-run rule exists to avoid. The newer run's own `completed` event is attempt 1 and is refused, so it cannot re-start the cancelled panel; only the re-run's panel survives.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. `ciPassed` (mark-ready.mjs:175-189) and `reviewChecks` (mark-ready.mjs:300-310) both `process.exit(2)` inside a bare catch around `execFileSync("gh", …)` (mark-ready.mjs:113-119) with no retry and no status-code discrimination — a 404 rename and a transient 503/network blip take the identical path, so the in-code comment's claimed distinction is not actually made. Exit 2 is routed by agent-review-panel.yml:1543 (`2) … exit 2`), failing the `promote` job; `stalled` fires on `needs.promote.result == 'failure'` (agent-review-panel.yml:2330), posts `<!-- agent-review-paged -->` with "The review panel will not run again on this PR" (line 2416) and reconciles to `agent:blocked` (lines 2460-2465). The `gate` job latches on that marker and sets `managed = false` (lines 233-250), so the autonomous loop is permanently stopped for that PR until a human runs `@claude rerun` (agent-rerun.yml:3-4, 145-176). The asymmetry is real and deliberate elsewhere: gate 1b's catch returns false → exit 1 → benign "leaving as draft" (mark-ready.mjs:274-285; agent-review-panel.yml:1541-1542). The same file documents that unretried API calls are known-fatal (retries:3 rationale, agent-review-panel.yml:915-932, citing a 4-minute 503 outage that killed three panel runs), yet these two reads have no retry. In-lane (error handling that mis-handles transient failures, leaving terminal/inconsistent loop state) and major: a single transient 5xx on a normal path ends the loop and requires manual human intervention. No guard makes it unreachable.

finding.summary: Gate 2 still swallows an unreadable check-runs API into "review not approved" (exit 1), the same silent-draft-forever failure this delta fixes for gate 1
finding.evidence: `reviewChecks` at lines 291-300: `try { data = ghJson(["api", `…/commits/${sha}/check-runs?per_page=100`]); } catch { return { allPassed: false, perCheck: … } }`. A transient 5xx/403/rate-limit or any gh failure on this read is reported as "the panel did not approve": the report prints ❌, the script exits 1, and the promote job in agent-review-panel.yml (line 1539-1542) sees the verdict line, records `outcome=gates-unsatisfied` and SUCCEEDS. Nothing re-runs the panel, so a PR whose gates were all actually green sits as a draft forever with no page — the exact reasoning the new catch at line 175-188 gives for gate 1. `set-state.mjs::gatherSignals` (lines 238-245) treats the identical read failure as `complete = false` rather than as a signal value, confirming the intended convention. Delta-exposed: gate 1 now exits 2 for its read failure while its sibling gate, reading the other unforgeable evidence on the same SHA, does not.

verdict.reason: The described swallow does not exist in the branch under review. In the working tree, scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:295-312 handles a check-runs read failure by printing "This is a tooling error, not a gate refusal — no review verdict was read." and calling process.exit(2) — it does NOT `return { allPassed: false, perCheck: ... }`. Consequently the exit-1 "gates not satisfied" path (:339-342) is never reached from this failure, the promote job cannot record gates-unsatisfied from an unreadable API, and the claimed asymmetry ("gate 1 now exits 2 while its sibling does not") is false: gate 1 (:175-189) and gate 2 (:300-310) both process.exit(2) with mutually cross-referencing comments, while gate 1b's `return false` (:274-285) is a documented, deliberate difference. The exact snippet the finding quotes appears only in the baseline copy at .trusted/scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:152-154, so the reviewer evidently read the pre-change file; the fix it asks for is already in the delta. set-state.mjs:238-245 is a different function whose output space includes "incomplete", so it does not establish a convention this code violates.

finding.summary: Gate 1b re-reads (pins) the head SHA but never re-reads the base ref — a base retarget landing between the base check and the file listing empties the list and the gate passes
finding.evidence: `ranBaseCiDefinition` reads `pr.baseRefName` from the snapshot taken at line 137-143 and compares it to `defaultBranch()` (line 231-237), then fetches `pulls/N/files` (line 239), then re-reads `headRefOid` (line 246) explicitly "so it covers the whole window in which the evidence was gathered". But `pulls/N/files` is computed by GitHub against the PR's base AT REQUEST TIME, and the base is never re-read. An author who flips the base from `main` to a branch that already carries the gutted CI definition after line 232 but before line 239 gets an empty/clean file list, the head-pin at line 246 still matches (no push happened), and gate 1b returns true. The gate's own comment (a) says the base is author-controlled and mutable, which is exactly why it is checked — yet the mutable-field pinning treatment given to the head is not given to the base. Fix: re-read `baseRefName` alongside `headRefOid` after the file listing.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: `pr.baseRefName` is read exactly once, in the snapshot at mark-ready.mjs:137-143, and compared against a live `defaultBranch()` at line 244 — before `pulls/N/files` is fetched at line 211 (via `ciDefiningPathsChanged`, called at 251). The post-listing re-read at line 258 covers only `headRefOid`. I enumerated every `gh` read in the file (137, 171, 211, 229, 258, 299, 384): nothing re-reads the base, no `pulls/N` full object, no `base.sha`, no merge-base comparison. Repo-wide greps for `baseRefName`/`base_ref`/`base.sha`/`default_branch` found no other guard on the promote path, and the invoking `promote` job (.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1453-1550) only branches on the exit code — it has no `base.ref` condition, and no workflow triggers on a base-retarget (`edited`) event. Tests at mark-ready.test.mjs:432-476 cover a static stacked base, a renamed default branch, a missing `default_branch`, and `headAfter`, but no mid-gate base change. The staleness window is in fact wider than claimed, since the base value dates from before gate 1's API reads. A retarget inside that window yields a file list computed against a different base while the head-pin still matches, so gate 1b returns true on evidence about a comparison it never made — an ordering/TOCTOU defect in the gate's own pinning logic, reachable non-adversarially by a human retargeting a stacked PR mid-run.

finding.summary: `ciRunToRerun` can select a run that is not the run gate 1 reads, producing a panel round that can never promote and no further admissible panel event
finding.evidence: `ciRunToRerun` returns the newest COMPLETED run, while `ciConclusion` (gate 1, mark-ready.mjs:178) returns the newest run by id regardless of status, and the panel's `ci` job (agent-review-panel.yml:300-336) reads the TRIGGERING run. When a head SHA carries two runs (close/reopen files a second `pull_request` run — the docstring at checks.mjs:165-170 acknowledges this) and the newer one is still in flight, `@claude rerun` re-runs the older finished run. That emits `completed` with `run_attempt > 1`, which the panel gate admits; the panel's `ci` job sees that run succeed and promote runs; but mark-ready's gate 1 reads the NEWER (in-flight) run, gets `null`, and exits 1 ("leaving as draft"). The newer run's own `completed` event arrives with `run_attempt == 1` and is REFUSED by the panel gate (agent-review-panel.yml:168-169), so no further panel round is admitted and the PR sits as a draft — the exact failure mode the comment at agent-review-panel.yml:1454-1461 exists to prevent. The docstring's claim that "gate 1 reads whichever ends up newest when it next runs" assumes a next panel round that the gate does not admit.

verdict.reason: All cited code is present exactly as described. `ciRunToRerun` (checks.mjs:231-233) selects the newest COMPLETED run, while gate 1's `ciConclusion` (checks.mjs:193-203, used by mark-ready.mjs:190) selects the newest run by id regardless of status and yields null for an in-flight one (pinned by mark-ready.test.mjs:541-546). The panel's `ci` job polls only the TRIGGERING run (agent-review-panel.yml:300-326), and the panel gate refuses a fresh run's own `completed`/attempt-1 event (agent-review-panel.yml:164-169), while the concurrency partition (115-118) puts the rerun round and the newer run's `requested` round in the same `active` cancel-in-progress group, so the round waiting on the newer run is cancelled. Result: the rerun round's promote reads a null gate 1, exits 1, logs "leaving as draft" and SUCCEEDS (1539-1540) — precisely the stall the comment at 1455-1461 says must not happen — with no admissible follow-up round. I found no guard and no scheduled retry (mark-ready is invoked only from agent-review-panel.yml), and both inline mirrors (agent-rerun.yml:200-205, agent-loop.yml:156-161) share the completed-only rule without refusing when a newer run is in flight. The window is narrow (close/reopen producing a second run that is still in flight when `@claude rerun` fires and remains in flight past the panel round), which bears on likelihood, not reachability; nothing lets me show it unreachable or already guarded.
